title: Ethiopian Lentil and Spinach Stew
localName: ምስር ስፒናጭ ወጥ — Misir Spinach Wat
community: Modern Ethiopian cooking — combined lentil and green stew
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Lentil and Spinach Stew — red lentils cooked in a berbere sauce with spinach added in the final 5 minutes. The nutritionally supercharged Misir Wat — the combination of lentil iron with spinach iron and vitamin C for maximum absorption.
longDesc: Lentil and spinach stew takes Misir Wat and adds the nutritional power of spinach — both are very high in iron, and the spinach's vitamin C dramatically improves the iron bioavailability of the lentils. A modern nutritional upgrade to the classic dish.
steps: Make Misir Wat base (ETH101) through the simmering stage.
When lentils are almost done, add spinach.
Stir spinach into the hot lentil sauce.
chefTips: Add spinach at the very end — it only needs 3 minutes.
The spinach wilts dramatically — add generously.
cookingScience: Non-haem iron from lentils and spinach is poorly absorbed on its own — typically only 5—12% bioavailability. However, vitamin C in the spinach converts non-haem iron from Fe³⁺ to Fe²⁺, increasing absorption to 20—40%. Cooking the spinach briefly preserves much of its vitamin C while breaking down the cell walls to release the iron.
sustainabilityTips: Both lentils and spinach are among the most sustainable foods available.
culturalNote: Lentil and spinach stew demonstrates how Ethiopian fasting cuisine continues to evolve — taking the ancient berbere-lentil tradition and enriching it with modern nutritional understanding.
